brief:
Bitcoin Magazine published commentary arguing that decades of industrial offshoring have left the United States reliant on foreign competitors for critical technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. Craig Tindale drew parallels to historical figures Alexander Hamilton and Dwight Eisenhower in framing AI development as a matter of national defense strategy rather than commercial competition alone.

The piece contends that financial and industrial policy decisions have undermined domestic technological capacity, creating vulnerabilities that threaten national security interests in an era of advancing AI capabilities.
dek: Bitcoin Magazine Financial Repression in the Age of AI Offshoring left the U.S. dependent on rivals for critical tech, says Craig Tindale. Drawing on Hamilton & Eisenhower, he frames AI as a defense mandate.
title: U.S. tech dependence on rivals poses national security risk, analyst argues
